evals.prompt: Using the accessibility skill, review this button for accessibility: <button><svg><!-- menu icon --></svg></button>. What's wrong and how do you fix it?
evals.expected_output: Flags that the button has no accessible name (a screen reader user hears nothing meaningful), and recommends adding aria-label="Open menu" (or visually-hidden text) plus aria-hidden="true" on the decorative icon.

assertions.text: Flags the missing accessible name for the icon-only button
Recommends aria-label or visually-hidden text as the fix

evals.prompt:
Using the accessibility skill, review this for keyboard accessibility:
Open
. What's the problem, and what's the best fix?
evals.expected_output: Flags that a div with only a click handler is not focusable and has no keyboard activation, and recommends using a native <button> element instead of adding manual tabindex/role/keydown handling to the div.

assertions.text: Flags the div as not keyboard-accessible/focusable
Recommends a native button as the primary fix

evals.prompt: Using the accessibility skill, is this CSS accessible for normal body text: color: #999; background: #fff;? Why or why not, per WCAG?
evals.expected_output: Flags that #999 on #fff is roughly 2.5:1 contrast, well below the WCAG AA minimum of 4.5:1 for normal text, and recommends a darker color that meets or exceeds 4.5:1.

assertions.text: Flags this as failing the WCAG AA contrast minimum
Names the correct AA threshold for normal text
